traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Elaeocarpaceae with Muntingiaceae, Petenaeaceae, Tremandraceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves usually alternate, sometimes opposite or whorled; leaves simple; veins usually pinnate, sometimes palmate or single; stipules usually present, sometimes absent; plants hermaphrodite or dioecious; ovary usually superior, sometimes half inferior or inferior; floral cup absent; stems usually woody, sometimes herbaceous; flowers in panicles, in cymes or in racemes; flowers usually actinomorphic, sometimes zygomorphic; perianth usually sepals and petals, sometimes tepals; fruit capsule, drupe or berry; stamens 12 to 100; carpels (1-) 2 to 10. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.flower_merosity.note: APweb, Oxalidales page, Elaeocarpaceae (read 2026-10-16): flowers often 4-merous.

traits.sexual_system.note: Wikipedia Elaeocarpus (read 2026-10-17): ~480 spp, flowers usually bisexual. Elaeocarpus is well over half the family (Sloanea next at ~150, Wikipedia Sloanea, sex not stated there). Dioecy is confined to smaller genera such as Aristotelia.

traits.inflorescence.note: Wikipedia Elaeocarpus (read 2026-10-17): ~480 spp with flowers usually in racemes, well over half the family. Sloanea (~150, Wikipedia Sloanea) is not counted as its page gives no inflorescence; panicles and cymes stay for the remaining genera.

traits.fruit_type.note: Wikipedia Elaeocarpus (read 2026-10-17): fruit an oval to round, usually blue drupe; ~480 spp, the family's largest genus by far. Sloanea (~150 spp, Wikipedia Sloanea, fruit not stated there) and the Tetratheca group carry capsules, so capsule stays often; berries (Aristotelia, Muntingia) are fewer.
